items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: "I left my horn in Bill’s car the other night."

ctx.x: A boat ride would cost you what? If you took your family, was it – is it like going to the movies or . . . ? [?] how people treated you.

Something like that. Yeah. You could dance and listen to the music. But it too was racial. They had black boat rides and white boat rides. Everything was a two-way in those days. Matter of fact, when I first went on the road down South, we played dances. On certain days it would be for the whites and the blacks would sit in the balcony and watch. Then certain other days it would be for blacks, while whites sat in the balcony and watched. In areas where they didn’t have balconies, the facilities to segregate like…
Now, Dewey Jackson’s band – what did Dewey Jackson play?
